title: Cold rebuild: pgrep
summary: Rebuild pgrep from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **pgrep** in *Processes and signals*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The server is slow. Which command shows you, **live**, which process is eating the CPU?
steps.explain: `ps` is a snapshot; `top`/`htop` refresh continuously. `df -h` is disk space.

steps.title: Rebuild pgrep cold
prompt: Write `List<int> Pgrep(List<string> ps, string name)` over `ps -eo pid,ppid,user,cmd` output: the first line is the header; every other line has PID, PPID, USER and then the command (which may contain spaces), separated by one or more spaces and possibly leading spaces. Return the PIDs whose **command** contains `name`, in order.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
